items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president 1889-1911, creamery built 1891 - Story 1.
Article VII quoted verbatim, including the governing-station clause - Story 1.
'Under payment by weight, nothing that follows would have cost any man a dollar.' - Story 1.
Loomis secretary 1901, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker - all named in Story 1.
'Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager 1913-1938' - Story 1.

Station-gain line, its shape, the 1898 entry quoted verbatim, carried to the general account - Story 5. (The sheet also credits Teague with devising it in 1905; penalized as a separate corruption deduction, not here.)
Station seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass 'borrowing of Larrow Green' - Stories 2 and 3. 'Ostrey Hollow' appears in Section A only inside quoted documents.
Milk weighed in, per-patron composite jar made up over ten days, charge drawn to the mark on the stem, fat read in percent, cream down / skim back - Story 2.
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; into use 1 May 1897 - Story 3.
Invoice itemized in full, 6 doz. pipettes, stem blown 17.6, total $77.93 - Story 3.
'as much in July as in February, wet years and dry' on a 0.19 gap - Story 4.

LOST: Section A never states that the pipette is the one instrument that cannot be checked without a burette / was never verified. The claim is made only in F1, and Section A takes no credit from B-G.
b.1861 d. February 1934; twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924 (Story 2); dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 7).
Five columns named; 'errors struck through and initialed, never a figure over a figure' - Story 2.
Summary leaf quoted: 1896 3.80, 1897 part year, 1898 3.61, within three hundredths since. Both figures present.
Broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure, 3.80 through, fell the same day 10 July, question mark; nine weeks / 63 days - Story 2.
Orra nee Brant; Emmet her brother, largest farmer on Hessel Bottom and the station's largest patron - Story 6.
1919 circular over the manager's signature (Story 6); 17 March statement - tested as taught, could not tell them why, never took a pound of cream (Story 7).
Died February 1934 (Story 2); test book and crate to the Historical Rooms in 1959 (Story 8). Keyed bold is the 1934 death.
Six farms visited (Story 4); Emmet Brant the largest holder on the wet bottom (Story 6).
LOST: Section A names Brant's weigh book only as an exhibit and a record set. '1 January 1897' and 'my own scale and theirs agreeing' appear in C2 and E1(iii), never in Section A.
'From 1902 the Hollow men said their milk tested under the same class of milk at the Green.' (The sheet puts that visible gap at 0.19 rather than 0.17; the key makes that context, not a gate.)
Grigg committee, January-February-March 1908 sampling, the wet-hay conclusion given as the committee's finding and then refuted - Story 4.
LOST: Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb on a recorded 3.42) and the proportionality point (4.56 short 0.24, 3.42 short 0.18) are stated correctly in C1(a)/C2 and F1 - and nowhere in Section A.
'Emmet Brant's weigh book, lent by Roy Brant' among the five record sets Ivy assembled in 1958 - Story 8.
LOST: Section A gives no founding year; the sheet rules 1913-vs-1914 undeterminable. Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd are all present; the keyed 1914 is not.
'From 1915 four of the six Bottom men hauled ... in the flush', sixteen seasons to 1930 - Story 4.

LOST: Section A never states that Cudd tested on his own bench with his own glassware, kept his own test book, and never compared it with anybody's. It has 'an unintended control', Vessey County and Rosalie's copied table.
Same herds ran 3.78-3.82 every summer, mean about 3.80, while running 3.61 at home, sixteen seasons - Story 4.
Same herds, same wet ground, same summers, two buildings (Story 4); and Cudd as the defeater of the watering charge (Story 6).
'Jerome Cudd and his daughter Rosalie' (Story 4); 'the Alder Corners figures, copied for her by Rosalie Cudd' in 1958 (Story 8); sixteen-season table.
LOST: circuit given as 1907-1936. The key requires 1908-1936; the sheet resolves the conflict the other way, on Strawn's own covering note.
Scales true at every visit for thirty years, never found added water, told the manager so in 1919 - Stories 2 and 6.
12 June 1923, run against a burette, condemned the whole crate - Story 3.
LOST: Section A does not say he wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation, nor that he drew no inference.
Order 28 June, Ammon's letter of 2 July, new glass in use from July; 1924 average 3.80 (Story 2); nobody connected it (Stories 5 and 7).
'up the ladder into the loft and stayed thirty-five years' (Story 3); 'Strawn's circuit books, unasked-for at Farland since 1947' (Story 8).

LOST: the January 1925 petition is dated correctly, but Section A attributes it to the long-standing Hollow-vs-Green comparison and never to the 1924 rise - which is this item's distinct aspect under the no-double-count rule.
Frick chairman, three sessions, first 17 March 1925, reported 4 May, second and third in the station's own weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (the 1908 report); 'None was proved and none accepted.'
Four exhibits named, including Strawn's 1923 notebook; 'Nobody laid one beside another and looked.'
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding then or ever; 4 May award of $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account.

'The award was one fifth of what was owed'; $19,000 and the 76,000 lb station-gain accumulation both stated in Story 5; award charged to the station account, which Story 5 names as the station-gain ledger.
Ivy b.1931, Duncan's daughter and Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland under Vaught.
'five sets of records, no two ever in one room before', all five named.
February 1958, up a ladder to the loft, crate under a tarpaulin, nine unbroken pipettes.
9 March 1958, nine readings listed, mean 16.72 against a blown 17.6, short 0.88, ninety-five hundredths of the mark.
Bulletin quote gives 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 at one part in twenty; 3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80; the 0.19 in Story 4.

76,000 lb and $19,000 in Stories 5 and 8, explicitly identified with the ledger's station-gain entries. Milk given as 1,600,000 lb a year over 1898-1922 rather than a 40,000,000 total; credited on substance (same quantity, per-year form). No corrupted value carried.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, quoted and clearing him; thirty-five / thirty-three / twenty-four years all stated.
Granddaughter.
Ansel -> Duncan -> Ivy, from r18/r04/r24; the great-niece carriers identified and Falke's own retraction cited.
Second cousins, derived: Orra/Emmet siblings -> Duncan/Roy first cousins -> Ivy/Hazel.

Filed under 'what the sources leave open', with the half-sibling case noted not to change the degree - the keyed answer, in the section where the question is put. (E1(iii) resolves it 'Full'; collision flagged, no deduction taken.)
Gideon Vose, his father, first president, who drafted the by-laws.
Gideon wrote Article VII, so the manager pressing the watering charge was enforcing his own father's rule against the consequences of the instrument that rule made decisive.
'No relationship ... is established' plus 'Strictly, a negative cannot be proved from these sources' - a lean with an explicit declination, protected by the key's own clause.
Two self-declared rumors (both narrators label their own evidence hearsay), one flat family denial, no document in the corpus naming a tie.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95 exactly; 0.88 / 17.6 = 0.05; 95 per cent of truth, one part in twenty.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80; short 0.19; confirmed six independent ways.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; $3,800 / $19,000 = 0.20 = one fifth. Both money and fraction given.
3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60; 7,200 lb; owed 360 lb, with a check line.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, and the sheet states why 24c and not the 25c period average.
40,000,000 x 3.80% = 1,520,000 lb, cross-checked against 25 x the ledger's 60,800.
5.00% of delivered and 5.263% of credited, denominators named explicitly and the ledger's 'five and a quarter' attached to the credited figure.
72 pipettes (six dozen, 'which only works at 72'), each short 0.88 c.c. Both required elements present.

1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 = 26 years 1 month 11 days (an accepted exact equivalent) against 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, with the part-year reason given. The extra 'less the nine weeks of 1911' refinement does not displace either keyed figure.
A02 abstention: 'Cannot be determined from the sources', with the ledger gap, both undocumented recollections and their spread.
Variable named as the measure that drew the charge, with both dated entries.
Held constant: patrons, herds, ground, season, feed, acid, bottles, hand tester, scales, operator - far more than three.
Rose to 3.80, held nine weeks (63 days), fell back to 3.61 on the day the station's own measure returned.
Establishes the field reversal that a calculation cannot, and states four limits (size over the period, direction, which property of the glass, the money) plus the undeterminable lender.
Four reasons, each tied to a named record and narrator: Sill's receiving book, Teague's ledger with Rundle's retraction, the 1911 interval, the constant fraction.
Independence argued record-by-record and man-by-man; reasons 1, 2 and 4 named as surviving without the 1958 burette.
A09: 'On the record, no', then 'Whether the 1916 conversation happened cannot be determined', with both poles and their weaknesses - a lean with an explicit declination.
LOST: answers the question with a definite verdict - 'Yes - unambiguously, and he said so himself.' The key makes D3 abstention item A03; asserting scores 0 and takes -2.

Cites manager from 1913, signing the station-gain sheets for twenty-five years, the 1919 circular, the grievance since 1902, and (in F) arguing watering in 1925. Misses only the keyed observation that nothing in Vose's hand ever names the glassware.

LOST: gives Teague-vs-Kyle and 'Signing is not reading', but does not state that neither cites a document, and directly contradicts the keyed point that no statement by Vose survives on what he knew before June 1923 - it uses the 1926 address as proof that he did.

Capped. At least eleven of the key's sixteen resolvable conflicts found, resolved correctly and with a method: Keddie's start, the 1908 sampling, the 1924 average, the weigh book, six farms, Orra's birth year, the crate's find-place, Ammon in Ordell, the swapped keepers, nine families, sixteen seasons, Vose from 1913. Missed: the cheese factory's year, Strawn's first year, the station-gain line's origin, r19's welding of 1908 to 1925.
Capped. E1(i) is a nineteen-row table of two-narrator wrong values with the tie-breaker named in each, including all four of the key's highest-value pairs (NT-1, NT-11, NT-14, NT-19).

Capped. A04 (the short lot; works records burned 1931), A06 (the borrowed measure; r09's pole impossible on the dates yet no lender named), A10 (the year of Article VII; minute book lost in the 1938 move) all declared unsettleable with what they do establish.
Sixteen self-refuting narrators listed with the specific page contradiction, including r05, r07, r11, r13, r15, r18 and r20.
Buckets sum to 10; the section is capped at 8.

Cause, size and mechanism all derived: 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.95, the neck ruled for a fixed charge, 0.19 as 5 per cent of 3.80 and not a constant, onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 against the 1924 3.80, and nothing changing on the farms at either end.
Watering named to Vose (and Sill in E) and defeated with the lactometer record, the cheesemaker's curd, Sill's heavy cream, the constancy, and the 1911 interval.

Theft named to Teague (and Toland/Oram in E) and defeated by the accuser's own ledger - stolen cream arrives light and this arrived heavy for twenty-five years - plus 1911 and the exact constant fraction.
Bog hay named to Grigg's 1908 committee and Kepp and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, the flat 0.19, Alder Corners, and the three-month sampling.
LOST: A07 answered with a flat 'No', and the sheet goes further, asserting that what the board saw tried was the 1923 replacement glass. Scores 0 and takes -2.

LOST: A05 answered 'The glass', with Frick's account expressly rejected and Ivy's statement called wrong. The later 'neither can be eliminated' does not undo a delivered verdict. Scores 0 and takes -2.
146 words, inside the 150-word limit.
Seven of the nine record series named: by-laws, tester's book, invoice, inspector's condemnation, cheese factory, ledger line, the 1919 circular, the hearing, the 1958 measurement.
LOST: neither Ansel Keddie nor Ivy Keddie is named - 'the tester's book' and 'a granddaughter with a burette'.
LOST: 1897, 76,000 lb and $19,000 are all there and no corruption is absorbed, but the summary gives neither the 1923 condemnation year (nor that it was accidental) nor the 1958 explanation year.
